feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Evidence from iteration 1 (the last race): all 60 trials ended off track with no finishes. Oval progress was 0.47 (up from 0.14 in iteration 0), max_error was 0.061 to 0.066 m on all three tracks, rms_error stayed at 0.026 to 0.031 m, and steering_oscillation rose to 0.28 on the oval. This pattern says the robot tracks well until one excursion at a bend pushes max_error past the 0.06 m off-track limit, so the sensor array is saturating at the edge. I made one controller change for your array: the weights are extended to seven values, [-2, -1.33, -0.67, 0, 0.67, 1.33, 2], keeping the iteration-1 signal scale and the kp 2.5, kd 0.30 gains. I have no per-step telemetry, so I cannot say where the first off-track event occurs, and I cannot yet say whether the 16 mm footprint degrades centre tracking. Change the next design depending on what the race shows. If max_error drops below 0.06 m on the oval and s-bend with line_loss_events near zero, keep the seven-sensor array and the 16 mm footprint, and test wheel_radius or base_speed for progress. If max_error stays at or above 0.06 m while steering_oscillation is below about 0.3, the array is still not the limit; the next step is a sensor lead change rather than more spread. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.3 and rms_error rises with it, the footprint is probably adding jitter, so test a smaller footprint before adding sensors.
requested_changes: If max_error is still at or above 0.06 m on the oval or s-bend while steering_oscillation stays below about 0.3, keep the seven-sensor spread and set mass to 0.7 kg (from 0.6). Iteration 1 showed max_error of 0.064 to 0.066 m on the oval and s-bend with small rms_error, so the excursion is a bend overshoot that more yaw inertia should damp.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.3 (iteration 1 reached 0.28 on the oval) and rms_error rises with it, set sensor_size to 0.012 (from 0.016) with the same seven positions. This tests whether the larger footprint adds centre jitter, a question the Builder raised and no race has answered yet.

If the robot holds the line (max_error below 0.06 m) but oval progress stays below 0.5, set wheel_radius to 0.04 m (from 0.035). Iteration 1 showed progress was limited by speed on the oval (0.47), and the 3.0 s limit needs an average speed near 1.5 m/s.
